This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants under Section 54(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'LA Act') for enhancement of the compensation granted by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mysuru in LACA No.111/2016 dated 29.07.2016.
2.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that the claimants are the owners of the land measuring 36  guntas in Sy.Nos.99/1, 94/21, 94/2 and 92 situated at Rammanahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Mysuru Taluk which came to be acquired by the respondents for the purpose of Varuna Canal Project, under a preliminary notification dated 27.08.1997 and final notification dated 18.06.1998.
The Land Acquisition Officer passed an award on 30.11.1998 determining the market value of the acquired land at Rs.60,000/- per acre.
Being aggrieved by the NC: 2023:KHC:28061 same, the claimants filed an application under Section 18(1) of the LA Act.
The same has been referred to the Reference Court and it has been numbered as LAC No.501/2004.

On consideration of the arguments of the parties and the materials available on record, the Reference Court by judgment and award dated 04.12.2010 enhanced the compensation from Rs.60,000/- to Rs.4,27,167/- per acre.
Being aggrieved by the same, for further enhancement, the claimants have filed an appeal before the District and Sessions Judge, Mysuru in LACA No.111/2016.
The appellate court, by judgment and award dated 29.07.2016 enhanced the compensation from Rs.4,27,167/- to Rs.6,50,000/-.
Being aggrieved by the same, for further enhancement claimants have filed this second appeal.

3. The learned counsel appearing for the claimants has contended that for the very same purpose,
adjacent land in the very same village has been acquired by the respondents by preliminary notification dated 27.08.1997.
NC: 2023:KHC:28061 The Reference Court in LAC No.512/1998 has determined the compensation at Rs.17,30,000/- per acre by judgment dated 20.07.2011.
Hence, he contended that the claimants are also entitled for enhancement of compensation in terms of the award passed by the Reference Court in LAC No.512/1998.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.

4. Per contra, learned Government Pleader appearing for the State has not disputed that the adjacent land has been acquired for the very same purpose by preliminary notification dated 27.08.1997 and the Reference Court in LAC No.512/1998 has awarded Rs.17,30,000/- per acre.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the original records.
6.
It is not in dispute that the claimants are the owners of the land measuring 36  guntas in Sy.Nos.99/1, 94/21, 94/2 and 92 situated at Rammanahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Mysuru Taluk.

It is also not in dispute that the said land has been acquired by NC: 2023:KHC:28061 the respondents Smt Indramma vs The Special Land on 8 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99798422/
3 for the purpose of Varuna Canal Project under a preliminary notification dated 27.08.1997 and final notification dated 18.06.1998.

The Land Acquisition Officer passed an award fixing the market value at Rs.60,000/- per acre and the Reference Court enhanced the compensation from Rs.60,000/- to Rs.4,27,167/- per acre and the appellate court further enhanced the compensation from Rs.4,27,167/- to Rs.6,50,000/- per acre.

7. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants has produced the judgment passed by the Reference court in LAC No.512/1998, wherein the adjacent land has been acquired for the very same purpose under preliminary notification dated 27.08.1997.
In the said case, the Reference Court has fixed the compensation at Rs.17,30,000/- per acre.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that the said judgment has attained finality as the respondents have not challenged the same.
In respect of grant of compensation by the Reference Court in LAC No.512/1998, the same has not been disputed by the learned Government Pleader.

9. Taking into consideration the place where the property is situated, submissions of the learned counsel appearing for the appellants and the materials available on record, I am of the opinion that the market value of the acquired land has to be enhanced from Rs.6,50,000/- to Rs.17,30,000/- per acre.

10. Accordingly, I pass the following order:
(i) Appeal is allowed in part with costs.
(ii) The compensation determined by the District and Sessions Judge, Mysuru at Rs.6,50,000/- is enhanced to Rs.17,30,000/- with all other consequential benefits.
